lines: 佛在舍衛國祇樹給孤獨園
與大比丘眾千二百五十人俱
爾時世尊食時著衣持缽
於其城中次第乞已還至本處
chapters.translation_en: Thus have I heard concerning our Lord Buddha:— Upon a memorable occasion, the Lord Buddha sojourned in the kingdom of Shravasti, lodging in the grove of Jeta, a park within the imperial domain, which Jeta, the heir-apparent, bestowed upon Sutana, a benevolent Minister of State, renowned for his charities and benefactions. With the Lord Buddha, there were assembled together twelve hundred and fifty mendicant disciples, all of whom had attained to eminent degrees of spiritual wisdom. As it approached the hour for the morning meal, Lord Buddha, Honoured of the Worlds, attired himself in a mendicant’s robe, and bearing an alms-bowl in his hands, walked towards the great city of Shravasti, which he entered to beg for food. Within the city he proceeded from door to door, and received such donations as the good people severally bestowed. Concluding this religious exercise, the Lord Buddha returned to the grove of Jeta, and partook of the frugal meal received as alms. Thereafter he divested himself of his mendicant’s robe, laid aside the venerated alms-bowl, bathed his sacred feet, and accepted the honoured seat reserved for him by his disciples.

en.plain: Your days are all the same round, the commute, the meals, the washing, and you wonder whether anything in them matters.
en.story:
The sutra opens with nothing happening. The Buddha puts on his robe, takes his bowl, walks into the city, begs from door to door in order, comes back, eats, puts the bowl away, washes his feet, and sits down. That is the whole first section. No teaching yet, no miracle.

The commentators have always said the teaching is already in it. The most ordinary round of a day, done with complete attention and no haste, is what the rest of the sutra will describe in harder words. For someone whose days are the same round, this section is a way of seeing them: not as the time before the real thing, but as the real thing, done in order, one door at a time.
en.reminder: The ordinary round, done in order, is the teaching.
en.acting: Do one part of today's round, the meal, the washing, the walk, at its own pace and with nothing else running.

zh_hant.plain: 你的日子都是同一個循環，通勤、吃飯、洗衣，你懷疑裡面有什麼要緊。
zh_hant.story:
這部經以「什麼都沒發生」開場。佛穿上衣，拿起缽，走進城裡，按次序一家一家乞食，回來，吃飯，收好缽，洗腳，坐下。這就是整個第一分。還沒有教法，沒有神蹟。

註解的人一直說，教法已經在裡面了。一天最平常的循環，用完整的注意力、不急地做，正是這部經接下來要用更難的話描述的東西。對一個日子都是同一個循環的人，這一分是看它們的一種方式：不是真正的事情之前的時間，而就是真正的事情，按次序做，一次一家。
zh_hant.reminder: 平常的循環，按次序做，就是教法。
zh_hant.acting: 今天循環裡的一部分，吃飯、洗衣、走路，用它自己的速度做，不同時跑別的事。

zh_hans.plain: 你的日子都是同一个循环，通勤、吃饭、洗衣，你怀疑里面有什么要紧。
zh_hans.story:
这部经以「什么都没发生」开场。佛穿上衣，拿起钵，走进城里，按次序一家一家乞食，回来，吃饭，收好钵，洗脚，坐下。这就是整个第一分。还没有教法，没有神迹。

注解的人一直说，教法已经在里面了。一天最平常的循环，用完整的注意力、不急地做，正是这部经接下来要用更难的话描述的东西。对一个日子都是同一个循环的人，这一分是看它们的一种方式：不是真正的事情之前的时间，而就是真正的事情，按次序做，一次一家。
zh_hans.reminder: 平常的循环，按次序做，就是教法。
zh_hans.acting: 今天循环里的一部分，吃饭、洗衣、走路，用它自己的速度做，不同时跑别的事。

lines: 時長老須菩提在大眾中
即從座起偏袒右肩右膝著地
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心
如汝所說如來善護念諸菩薩
汝今諦聽當為汝說善男子
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心
應如是住如是降伏其心
chapters.translation_en: Upon that occasion, the venerable Subhuti occupied a place in the midst of the assembly. Rising from his seat, with cloak arranged in such manner that his right shoulder was disclosed, Subhuti knelt upon his right knee, then pressing together the palms of his hands, he respectfully raised them towards Lord Buddha, saying: “Thou art of transcendent wisdom, Honoured of the Worlds! With wonderful solicitude, Thou dost preserve in the faith, and instruct in the Law, this illustrious assembly of enlightened disciples. Honoured of the Worlds! if a good disciple, whether man or woman, seeks to obtain supreme spiritual wisdom, what immutable Law shall sustain the mind of that disciple, and bring into subjection every inordinate desire?” The Lord Buddha replied to Subhuti, saying: “Truly a most excellent theme! As you affirmed, I preserve in the faith, and instruct in the Law, this illustrious assembly of enlightened disciples. Attend diligently unto me, and I shall enunciate a Law whereby the mind of a good disciple, whether man or woman, seeking to obtain supreme spiritual wisdom, shall be adequately sustained, and enabled to bring into subjection every inordinate desire.” Subhuti was gratified, and signified glad consent. Thereupon, the Lord Buddha, with majesty of person, and perfect articulation, proceeded to deliver the text of this Scripture, saying:—

en.plain: You want to be a better person, calmer, kinder, and you have no idea where to put your mind to begin.
en.story:
Subhuti stands up, bares his right shoulder, kneels, and asks the question the whole sutra answers: when a person sets out toward awakening, how should they settle their mind, and how should they subdue it? The Buddha says: good, listen.

The question is a good one because it is practical. Not what is awakening, but where do I put my mind on a Tuesday. Everyone who has wanted to be calmer has asked it, usually without the ceremony. The section's answer is only 'listen', and that is not evasion: the rest of the sutra is the answer, and it begins by taking the question seriously enough to make the questioner sit down for it.
en.reminder: Where do I put my mind? is the right question.
en.acting: Write the question in your own words, in one line, and keep it where the answer will find it.

zh_hant.plain: 你想當一個更好的人，更平靜、更善良，卻不知道該把心放在哪裡開始。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提站起來，露出右肩，跪下，問了整部經在回答的那個問題：一個人發心走向覺悟，該怎麼安住他的心，該怎麼降伏它？佛說：好，你聽。

這個問題好，因為它實際。不是「什麼是覺悟」，而是「星期二我該把心放在哪裡」。每一個想更平靜的人都問過它，通常沒有這麼隆重。這一分的回答只有「聽」，那不是迴避：接下來整部經都是回答，而回答的開始，是把這個問題看得夠認真，讓問的人為它坐下來。
zh_hant.reminder: 「我該把心放在哪裡？」是對的問題。
zh_hant.acting: 用你自己的話把這個問題寫成一行，放在答案找得到它的地方。

zh_hans.plain: 你想当一个更好的人，更平静、更善良，却不知道该把心放在哪里开始。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提站起来，露出右肩，跪下，问了整部经在回答的那个问题：一个人发心走向觉悟，该怎么安住他的心，该怎么降伏它？佛说：好，你听。

这个问题好，因为它实际。不是「什么是觉悟」，而是「星期二我该把心放在哪里」。每一个想更平静的人都问过它，通常没有这么隆重。这一分的回答只有「听」，那不是回避：接下来整部经都是回答，而回答的开始，是把这个问题看得够认真，让问的人为它坐下来。
zh_hans.reminder: 「我该把心放在哪里？」是对的问题。
zh_hans.acting: 用你自己的话把这个问题写成一行，放在答案找得到它的地方。

lines: 佛告須菩提諸菩薩摩訶薩
所有一切眾生之類若卵生
我皆令入無餘涅槃而滅度之
如是滅度無量無數無邊眾生
若菩薩有我相人相眾生相
chapters.translation_en: “By this wisdom shall enlightened disciples be enabled to bring into subjection every inordinate desire! Every species of life, whether hatched in the egg, formed in the womb, evolved from spawn, produced by metamorphosis, with or without form or intelligence, possessing or devoid of natural instinct—from these changeful conditions of being, I command you to seek deliverance, in the transcendental concept of Nirvana. Thus, you shall be delivered from an immeasurable, innumerable, and illimitable world of sentient life; but, in reality, there is no world of sentient life from which to seek deliverance. And why? Because, in the minds of enlightened disciples there have ceased to exist such arbitrary concepts of phenomena as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality.” “Moreover, Subhuti, an enlightened disciple ought to act spontaneously in the exercise of charity, uninfluenced by sensuous phenomena such as sound, odour, taste, touch, or Law. Subhuti, it is imperative that an enlightened disciple, in the exercise of charity, should act independently of phenomena. And why? Because, acting without regard to illusive forms of phenomena, he will realise in the exercise of charity, a merit inestimable and immeasurable.” “Subhuti, what think you? Is it possible to estimate the distance comprising the illimitable universe of space?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! It is impossible to estimate the distance comprising the illimitable universe of space.” The Lord Buddha thereupon discoursed, saying: “It is equally impossible to estimate the merit of an enlightened disciple, who discharges the exercise of charity, unperturbed by the seductive influences of phenomena. Subhuti, the mind of an enlightened disciple ought thus to be indoctrinated.”

en.plain: You help people all day, family, colleagues, strangers, and you keep a quiet count of who has been helped.
en.story:
The Buddha answers: a bodhisattva resolves to bring every kind of being to liberation, and yet, having liberated countless beings, knows that no being was liberated. Why? Because if a bodhisattva holds the idea of a self, a person, a being, a life, they are not a bodhisattva.

The section is not against helping; it begins with the largest possible resolution to help. It is against the count. The moment the helper keeps a tally of beings helped, there is a self doing the helping and a person being helped, and the help has become a transaction. The quiet count is what makes helping tiring. Drop the count, and the same acts weigh less; the people helped are not entries, and neither are you.
en.reminder: Help everyone; count no one.
en.acting: Help one person today and then deliberately forget to add it to any list.

zh_hant.plain: 你整天在幫人，家人、同事、陌生人，心裡悄悄記著誰被幫過。
zh_hant.story:
佛回答：菩薩發願把一切眾生都度到解脫，而度了無數眾生之後，知道沒有一個眾生被度。為什麼？因為菩薩若有我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相，就不是菩薩。

這一分不反對幫人；它以最大可能的幫人的願開始。它反對的是那本帳。幫的人一記帳，就有一個在幫的自己和一個被幫的人，幫就變成了交易。悄悄記著的帳，正是讓幫人變累的東西。把帳丟掉，同樣的事變輕；被幫的人不是條目，你也不是。
zh_hant.reminder: 幫每一個人；不記任何一個。
zh_hant.acting: 今天幫一個人，然後故意忘記把它加進任何清單。

zh_hans.plain: 你整天在帮人，家人、同事、陌生人，心里悄悄记着谁被帮过。
zh_hans.story:
佛回答：菩萨发愿把一切众生都度到解脱，而度了无数众生之后，知道没有一个众生被度。为什么？因为菩萨若有我相、人相、众生相、寿者相，就不是菩萨。

这一分不反对帮人；它以最大可能的帮人的愿开始。它反对的是那本帐。帮的人一记帐，就有一个在帮的自己和一个被帮的人，帮就变成了交易。悄悄记着的帐，正是让帮人变累的东西。把帐丢掉，同样的事变轻；被帮的人不是条目，你也不是。
zh_hans.reminder: 帮每一个人；不记任何一个。
zh_hans.acting: 今天帮一个人，然后故意忘记把它加进任何清单。

lines: 菩薩於法應無所住行於布施
所謂不住色布施不住聲香味
菩薩應如是布施不住於相
南西北方四維上下虛空
福德亦復如是不可思量

Every species of life, whether hatched in the egg, formed in the womb, evolved from spawn, produced by metamorphosis, with or without form or intelligence, possessing or devoid of natural instinct—from these changeful conditions of being, I command you to seek deliverance, in the transcendental concept of Nirvana. Thus, you shall be delivered from an immeasurable, innumerable, and illimitable world of sentient life; but, in reality, there is no world of sentient life from which to seek deliverance. And why? Because, in the minds of enlightened disciples there have ceased to exist such arbitrary concepts of phenomena as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality.” “Moreover, Subhuti, an enlightened disciple ought to act spontaneously in the exercise of charity, uninfluenced by sensuous phenomena such as sound, odour, taste, touch, or Law. Subhuti, it is imperative that an enlightened disciple, in the exercise of charity, should act independently of phenomena. And why? Because, acting without regard to illusive forms of phenomena, he will realise in the exercise of charity, a merit inestimable and immeasurable.” “Subhuti, what think you? Is it possible to estimate the distance comprising the illimitable universe of space?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! It is impossible to estimate the distance comprising the illimitable universe of space.” The Lord Buddha thereupon discoursed, saying: “It is equally impossible to estimate the merit of an enlightened disciple, who discharges the exercise of charity, unperturbed by the seductive influences of phenomena. Subhuti, the mind of an enlightened disciple ought thus to be indoctrinated.”

en.plain: You gave something, money, time, a favour, and you are watching to see what comes back.
en.story:
A bodhisattva should give without dwelling on anything: not on form, not on sound, smell, taste, touch or idea. Giving without dwelling on appearances: the merit of that cannot be measured, any more than the space to the east, or in any direction, can be measured.

The section is about giving with no thread attached, and it knows how rare that is. Most giving has a thread: the expectation of thanks, of return, of being seen as generous. The thread is what makes the wait afterwards, and the wait is what sours the gift. The sutra's measure is the sky: giving that dwells on nothing is as wide as space, because nothing has been kept back to hold the thread. The favour was given. Let go of the other end.
en.reminder: Give, and let go of the other end.
en.acting: Give one thing today and tell no one, including the person who receives it if you can manage that.

zh_hant.plain: 你給了一樣東西，錢、時間、一個人情，正在等看什麼會回來。
zh_hant.story:
菩薩應該無所住地布施：不住色，不住聲、香、味、觸、法。不住相的布施，它的福德不可思量，就像東方的虛空不可思量，任何方向的虛空都不可思量。

這一分講的是沒有線綁著的給，而它知道那多麼少見。多數的給都有一條線：期待謝，期待回報，期待被看成慷慨。那條線就是之後的等待，而等待讓禮物變酸。經的量尺是天空：無所住的給像虛空一樣寬，因為沒有留下任何東西來握著那條線。人情已經給了。把另一端放開。
zh_hant.reminder: 給，然後放開另一端。
zh_hant.acting: 今天給一樣東西，不告訴任何人，做得到的話連收的人也不告訴。

zh_hans.plain: 你给了一样东西，钱、时间、一个人情，正在等看什么会回来。
zh_hans.story:
菩萨应该无所住地布施：不住色，不住声、香、味、触、法。不住相的布施，它的福德不可思量，就像东方的虚空不可思量，任何方向的虚空都不可思量。

这一分讲的是没有线绑着的给，而它知道那多么少见。多数的给都有一条线：期待谢，期待回报，期待被看成慷慨。那条线就是之后的等待，而等待让礼物变酸。经的量尺是天空：无所住的给像虚空一样宽，因为没有留下任何东西来握着那条线。人情已经给了。把另一端放开。
zh_hans.reminder: 给，然后放开另一端。
zh_hans.acting: 今天给一样东西，不告诉任何人，做得到的话连收的人也不告诉。

lines: 如來所說身相即非身相
若見諸相非相即見如來
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha interrogated Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Is it possible that by means of his physical body, the Lord Buddha may be clearly perceived?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! It is impossible that by means of his physical body, the Lord Buddha may be clearly perceived. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha referred to as a physical body, is in reality not merely a physical body.” Thereupon the Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “Every form or quality of phenomena is transient and illusive. When the mind realises that the phenomena of life are not real phenomena, the Lord Buddha may then be clearly perceived.”

en.plain: You judge people, and yourself, by how they look, the clothes, the flat, the body, and it is exhausting.
en.story:
Can the Buddha be recognised by his bodily marks? No, says Subhuti; the marks the Buddha speaks of are not marks. The Buddha agrees: every mark is a passing appearance; see that the marks are not marks, and you see the Buddha.

The Buddha in this section has thirty-two beautiful marks, and he says they are not how to know him. That is a strong thing for a text to say about its own hero. For a person tired of judging and being judged by appearances, it is a release from the whole exercise: the marks were never the person, on any side. The tiredness is the cost of a measuring that measures nothing. Put the tape down, on yourself first.
en.reminder: The marks were never the person.
en.acting: Notice one judgement by appearance today, yours of someone or of yourself, and let it pass without acting on it.

zh_hant.plain: 你用外表評斷別人，也評斷自己，衣服、房子、身體，這很累。
zh_hant.story:
能不能靠身相認出佛？須菩提說，不能；佛說的身相不是身相。佛同意：一切的相都是暫時的顯現；看見相不是相，就看見佛。

這一分裡的佛有三十二種美好的相，而他說，那不是認識他的方式。一部經對自己的主角說這樣的話，是很強的。對一個厭倦了用外表評斷和被評斷的人，這是從整件事裡鬆開：相從來就不是那個人，哪一邊都不是。累，是一種什麼也量不到的量的代價。把尺收起來，先從自己開始。
zh_hant.reminder: 相從來就不是那個人。
zh_hant.acting: 今天注意一次憑外表的評斷，你對別人的或對自己的，讓它過去，不照它行動。

zh_hans.plain: 你用外表评断别人，也评断自己，衣服、房子、身体，这很累。
zh_hans.story:
能不能靠身相认出佛？须菩提说，不能；佛说的身相不是身相。佛同意：一切的相都是暂时的显现；看见相不是相，就看见佛。

这一分里的佛有三十二种美好的相，而他说，那不是认识他的方式。一部经对自己的主角说这样的话，是很强的。对一个厌倦了用外表评断和被评断的人，这是从整件事里松开：相从来就不是那个人，哪一边都不是。累，是一种什么也量不到的量的代价。把尺收起来，先从自己开始。
zh_hans.reminder: 相从来就不是那个人。
zh_hans.acting: 今天注意一次凭外表的评断，你对别人的或对自己的，让它过去，不照它行动。

lines: 頗有眾生得聞如是言說章句
以此為實當知是人不於一佛
二佛三四五佛而種善根
已於無量千萬佛所種諸善根
聞是章句乃至一念生淨信者
是諸眾生得如是無量福德
是諸眾生無復我相人相
是諸眾生若心取相則為著我
若取法相即著我人眾生壽者
若取非法相即著我人眾生
是故不應取法不應取非法
汝等比丘知我說法如筏喻者
chapters.translation_en: Subhuti enquired of the Lord Buddha, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! In future ages, when this scripture is proclaimed, amongst those beings destined to hear, shall any conceive within their minds a sincere, unmingled faith?” The Lord Buddha replied to Subhuti, saying: “Have no such apprehensive thought! Even at the remote period of five centuries subsequent to the Nirvana of the Lord Buddha, there will be many disciples observing the monastic vows, and assiduously devoted to good works. These, hearing this scripture proclaimed, will believe in its immutability, and similarly conceive within their minds a pure, unmingled faith. Besides, it is important to realise that faith thus conceived, is not exclusively in virtue of the insular thought of any particular Buddha, but because of its affiliation with the concrete thoughts of myriad Buddhas, throughout infinite ages. Therefore, amongst the beings destined to hear this Scripture proclaimed, many, by momentary reflection, will intuitively conceive a pure and holy faith.” “Subhuti, the Lord Buddha by his prescience, is perfectly cognisant of all such potential disciples, and for these also there is reserved an immeasurable merit. And why? Because, the minds of these disciples will not revert to such arbitrary concepts of phenomena as an entity, a being, a living being, a personality, qualities or ideas coincident with Law, or existing apart from the idea of Law. And why? Because, assuming the permanency and reality of phenomena, the minds of these disciples would be involved in such distinctive ideas as an entity, a being, a living being, and a personality. Affirming the permanency and reality of qualities or ideas coincident with Law, their minds would inevitably be involved in resolving these same definitions. Postulating the inviolate nature of qualities or ideas which have an existence apart from the Law, there yet remain to be explained these abstruse distinctions—an entity, a being, a living being, and a personality. Therefore, enlightened disciples ought not to affirm the permanency or reality of qualities or ideas coincident with Law, nor postulate as being of an inviolate nature, qualities or ideas having an existence apart from the concept of Law.” “Thus, we are enabled to appreciate the significance of those words which the Lord Buddha invariably repeated to his followers: ‘You disciples must realise that the Law which I enunciated, was presented before your minds in the simile of a raft. If the Law—having fulfilled its function in bearing you to the other shore (Nirvana)—with its coincident qualities and ideas must inevitably be abandoned, how much more inevitable must be the abandonment of qualities or ideas which have an existence apart from the Law?’”

en.plain: You wonder whether any of this old text can really mean anything to a person with your problems, now.
en.story:
Subhuti asks whether people in later ages, hearing these words, will believe them. The Buddha says yes: there will be people who keep to the practice and have faith, and their faith will rest on roots planted long ago. Then the raft: my teaching is like a raft; even the teaching is to be set down once across, how much more everything else.

The section is the sutra anticipating you, the reader in a later age, and answering the doubt directly. Yes, it says, this is for you. And then it hands you the raft image, which is the most practical thing in the book: use what carries you across the present river, and do not carry it on your back afterwards. That applies to this sutra, to any method, to the app in your hand.
en.reminder: Use the raft; do not carry it afterwards.
en.acting: Take one line from this text that carries you today, use it, and leave the rest on the bank.

zh_hant.plain: 你懷疑這麼老的一部經，對一個有你這種問題的現代人，真的能有什麼意義。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提問，後世的人聽到這些話，會相信嗎？佛說會：會有人持戒修福，會生信心，他們的信心來自很久以前種下的根。然後是筏：我的法像筏；連法都要在渡過之後捨下，何況其他。

這一分是經在預見你，後世的讀者，並直接回答那個懷疑。是的，它說，這是給你的。然後它把筏的畫面交給你，那是整本書裡最實際的東西：用能載你渡過眼前這條河的東西，渡過之後不要背在背上。這適用於這部經，適用於任何方法，也適用於你手上這個程式。
zh_hant.reminder: 用筏；渡過之後不要背著它。
zh_hant.acting: 從這部經裡取一句今天載得動你的，用它，其餘留在岸邊。

zh_hans.plain: 你怀疑这么老的一部经，对一个有你这种问题的现代人，真的能有什么意义。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提问，后世的人听到这些话，会相信吗？佛说会：会有人持戒修福，会生信心，他们的信心来自很久以前种下的根。然后是筏：我的法像筏；连法都要在渡过之后舍下，何况其他。

这一分是经在预见你，后世的读者，并直接回答那个怀疑。是的，它说，这是给你的。然后它把筏的画面交给你，那是整本书里最实际的东西：用能载你渡过眼前这条河的东西，渡过之后不要背在背上。这适用于这部经，适用于任何方法，也适用于你手上这个程序。
zh_hans.reminder: 用筏；渡过之后不要背着它。
zh_hans.acting: 从这部经里取一句今天载得动你的，用它，其余留在岸边。

lines: 如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
須菩提言如我解佛所說義
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Has the Lord Buddha really attained to supreme spiritual wisdom? Or has he a system of doctrine which can be specifically formulated?” Subhuti replied, saying: “As I understand the meaning of the Lord Buddha’s discourse, he has no system of doctrine which can be specifically formulated; nor can the Lord Buddha express, in explicit terms, a form of knowledge which can be described as supreme spiritual wisdom. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha adumbrated in terms of the Law, is transcendental and inexpressible. Being a purely spiritual concept, it is neither consonant with Law, nor synonymous with anything apart from the Law. Thus is exemplified the manner by which wise disciples and holy Buddhas, regarding intuition as the Law of their minds, severally attained to different planes of spiritual wisdom.”

en.plain: You have read every method for getting your life in order and none of them survives contact with a Tuesday.
en.story:
Did the Buddha attain a fixed awakening, or teach a fixed doctrine? Subhuti answers: as I understand it, there is no fixed thing called awakening, and no fixed teaching. What the Buddha teaches cannot be grasped or spoken; it is neither a thing nor not a thing. That is why the sages differ.

The person who reads every system and finds each one fails on a Tuesday is not failing at systems; they have discovered what this section says outright. Tuesdays differ. The tool that fits one does not fit the next, and the skill is not in finding the master tool but in picking, each morning, the small one that fits today. The sages differ because the days do.
en.reminder: No master tool; only the one that fits today.
en.acting: Choose one small tool that fits this particular day, use it, and keep no score.

zh_hant.plain: 你把每一套整頓人生的方法都讀過了，沒有一套撐得過一個星期二。
zh_hant.story:
佛有沒有得到一個固定的覺悟，有沒有說一個固定的法？須菩提答：依我的理解，沒有一個固定的東西叫覺悟，也沒有固定的法。佛所說的法，不可取、不可說；不是法，也不是非法。所以賢聖各不相同。

把每一套系統都讀過、發現每一套都在某個星期二失效的人，不是在系統上失敗；他發現的正是這一分直接說出來的事。星期二各不相同。合這一個的工具不合下一個，本事不在找到那把萬能的工具，而在每天早上挑那把合今天的小工具。賢聖各不相同，因為日子各不相同。
zh_hant.reminder: 沒有萬能的工具；只有合今天的那一把。
zh_hant.acting: 挑一把合今天的小工具，用它，不記分。

zh_hans.plain: 你把每一套整顿人生的方法都读过了，没有一套撑得过一个星期二。
zh_hans.story:
佛有没有得到一个固定的觉悟，有没有说一个固定的法？须菩提答：依我的理解，没有一个固定的东西叫觉悟，也没有固定的法。佛所说的法，不可取、不可说；不是法，也不是非法。所以贤圣各不相同。

把每一套系统都读过、发现每一套都在某个星期二失效的人，不是在系统上失败；他发现的正是这一分直接说出来的事。星期二各不相同。合这一个的工具不合下一个，本事不在找到那把万能的工具，而在每天早上挑那把合今天的小工具。贤圣各不相同，因为日子各不相同。
zh_hans.reminder: 没有万能的工具；只有合今天的那一把。
zh_hans.acting: 挑一把合今天的小工具，用它，不记分。

lines: 若人滿三千大千世界七寶以
若復有人於此經中受持
乃至四句偈等為他人說
及諸佛阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? If a benevolent person bestowed as alms, an abundance of the seven treasures sufficient to fill the universe, would there accrue to that person a considerable merit?” Subhuti replied, saying: “A very considerable merit, Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, what is referred to does not partake of the nature of ordinary merit, and in this sense the Lord Buddha made mention of a ‘considerable’ merit.” The Lord Buddha rejoined, saying: “If a disciple adhered with implicit faith to a stanza of this Scripture, and diligently explained it to others, the intrinsic merit of that disciple would be relatively greater. And why? Because, Subhuti, the holy Buddhas, and the Law by which they attained to supreme spiritual wisdom, severally owe their inception to the truth of this sacred Scripture. Subhuti, what is ordinarily termed the Buddhic Law, is not really a Law attributive to Buddha.”

en.plain: You have been generous with money, and it has not made you feel any better.
en.story:
If a person filled three thousand worlds with treasure and gave it all away, would the merit be great? Very great, says Subhuti, and yet the Buddha says merit is not merit, which is why it can be called great. But a person who keeps even four lines of this teaching and explains it to another has merit beyond that, because all awakening comes from this teaching, and yet what is called the teaching is not the teaching.

The section ranks the gift of understanding above the gift of treasure, and the person who has given money and felt nothing will recognise why. Money given can be given from the surface. Four lines understood and passed on cost something interior, and that is where the feeling of having given comes from. This is not a reason to stop giving money. It is a reason to also give the other thing.
en.reminder: Four lines understood outweigh a world of treasure.
en.acting: Explain one line you have understood to one person this week, in your own words.

zh_hant.plain: 你在錢上一直慷慨，它沒有讓你覺得好一點。
zh_hant.story:
如果一個人用珍寶裝滿三千大千世界，全部布施出去，福德多不多？很多，須菩提說，而佛說福德不是福德，所以才能叫多。但一個人哪怕只受持這部經的四句，並為別人解說，福德更勝過那些，因為一切覺悟都從這部經出來，而所謂的法，不是法。

這一分把「理解」的給放在「珍寶」的給之上，給了錢卻沒有感覺的人會認得為什麼。錢可以從表面給。理解了的四句話、傳給別人，花的是內在的東西，而「給了」的感覺就是從那裡來的。這不是不再給錢的理由。這是也給另一樣東西的理由。
zh_hant.reminder: 理解了的四句話，勝過一個世界的珍寶。
zh_hant.acting: 這星期用自己的話，向一個人解說你理解了的一句。

zh_hans.plain: 你在钱上一直慷慨，它没有让你觉得好一点。
zh_hans.story:
如果一个人用珍宝装满三千大千世界，全部布施出去，福德多不多？很多，须菩提说，而佛说福德不是福德，所以才能叫多。但一个人哪怕只受持这部经的四句，并为别人解说，福德更胜过那些，因为一切觉悟都从这部经出来，而所谓的法，不是法。

这一分把「理解」的给放在「珍宝」的给之上，给了钱却没有感觉的人会认得为什么。钱可以从表面给。理解了的四句话、传给别人，花的是内在的东西，而「给了」的感觉就是从那里来的。这不是不再给钱的理由。这是也给另一样东西的理由。
zh_hans.reminder: 理解了的四句话，胜过一个世界的珍宝。
zh_hans.acting: 这星期用自己的话，向一个人解说你理解了的一句。

lines: 須陀洹名為入流而無所入
斯陀含名一往來而實無往來
阿那含名為不來而實無不來
我得阿羅漢道即為著我人
我不作是念我是離欲阿羅漢
我若作是念我得阿羅漢道
世尊則不說須菩提是樂阿蘭
而名須菩提是樂阿蘭那行
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? May a Scrotapatti (having entered the stream which bears on to Nirvana) thus moralise within himself, ‘I have obtained the fruits commensurate with the merit of a Scrotapatti’?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, Scrotapatti is simply a descriptive term signifying ‘having entered the stream.’ A disciple who avoids the seductive phenomena of form, sound, odour, taste, touch, and Law, is named a Scrotapatti.” The Lord Buddha again enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? May a Sakridagami (who is subject only to one more reincarnation) thus muse within himself, ‘I have obtained the fruits consonant with the merit of a Sakridagami’?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, Sakridagami is merely a descriptive title denoting ‘only one more reincarnation’; but in reality there is no such condition as ‘only one more reincarnation,’ hence Sakridagami is merely a descriptive title.” The Lord Buddha once again enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? May an Anagami (having entire immunity from reincarnation) thus reflect within himself, ‘I have obtained the fruits which accord with the merit of an Anagami?’” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, Anagami is merely a designation meaning ‘immunity from reincarnation’; but in reality there is no such condition as ‘immunity from reincarnation,’ hence Anagami is merely a convenient designation.” The Lord Buddha yet again enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? May an Arhat (having attained to absolute quiescence of mind) thus meditate within himself, ‘I have obtained the condition of an Arhat’?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, there is not in reality a condition synonymous with the term Arhat. Honoured of the Worlds! if an Arhat thus meditates within himself, ‘I have obtained the condition of an Arhat,’ there would be obvious recurrence of such arbitrary concepts as an entity, a being, a living being, and a personality. Honoured of the Worlds! When the Lord Buddha declared that in absolute quiescence of mind, perfect observance of the Law, and true spiritual perception, I was pre-eminent amongst the disciples, I did not cogitate thus within myself, ‘I am an Arhat, freed from desire!’ Had I thus cogitated, ‘I have obtained the condition of an Arhat,’ the ‘Honoured of the Worlds’ would not have declared concerning me, ‘Subhuti delights in the austerities practised by the Aranyaka’; but, in reality, Subhuti was perfectly quiescent and oblivious to phenomena; hence the allusion, ‘Subhuti delights in the austerities practised by the Aranyaka.’”

en.plain: You reached a milestone, a degree, a promotion, a target, and you can feel it hardening into an identity.
en.story:
The Buddha asks about each stage of attainment in turn: does the stream-enterer think 'I have entered the stream'? No; if he did, he would be holding to a self. The same for each stage up to the arhat: does he think 'I have attained'? No, says Subhuti; if he did, it would not be attainment. Then Subhuti speaks of himself: the Buddha says I am foremost in stillness, yet I do not think 'I am foremost'; if I did, the Buddha would not say it.

The section is a ladder of achievements and the same instruction at every rung: do not hold it. A milestone becomes a self when it is held, and a held self has to be defended at the next milestone. Subhuti's example is the useful one: he really is foremost, and he really does not think it. The two are not in conflict. Have the achievement; do not become it.
en.reminder: Have the achievement; do not become it.
en.acting: Say your new title or milestone once today without the word 'I' in front of it, and see how it sits.

zh_hant.plain: 你到達了一個里程碑，學位、升遷、目標，你感覺得到它正在硬化成一種身分。
zh_hant.story:
佛依次問每一個果位：入流的人會不會想「我入了流」？不會；如果他想，就是執著一個我。每一個果位都一樣，直到阿羅漢：他會不會想「我得到了」？不會，須菩提說；如果他想，就不是得到。然後須菩提說自己：佛說我在寂靜上是第一，但我不想「我是第一」；如果我想，佛就不會這樣說。

這一分是一道成就的梯子，每一級都是同一個指令：不要抓住它。里程碑被抓住就變成一個自己，而被抓住的自己在下一個里程碑時就得被防衛。須菩提的例子是有用的：他真的是第一，他也真的不這樣想。兩者不衝突。擁有成就；不要變成它。
zh_hant.reminder: 擁有成就；不要變成它。
zh_hant.acting: 今天把你的新頭銜或里程碑說一次，前面不加「我」，看看它怎麼放。

zh_hans.plain: 你到达了一个里程碑，学位、升迁、目标，你感觉得到它正在硬化成一种身分。
zh_hans.story:
佛依次问每一个果位：入流的人会不会想「我入了流」？不会；如果他想，就是执着一个我。每一个果位都一样，直到阿罗汉：他会不会想「我得到了」？不会，须菩提说；如果他想，就不是得到。然后须菩提说自己：佛说我在寂静上是第一，但我不想「我是第一」；如果我想，佛就不会这样说。

这一分是一道成就的梯子，每一级都是同一个指令：不要抓住它。里程碑被抓住就变成一个自己，而被抓住的自己在下一个里程碑时就得被防卫。须菩提的例子是有用的：他真的是第一，他也真的不这样想。两者不冲突。拥有成就；不要变成它。
zh_hans.reminder: 拥有成就；不要变成它。
zh_hans.acting: 今天把你的新头衔或里程碑说一次，前面不加「我」，看看它怎么放。

lines: 不應住色生心不應住聲香味
觸法生心應無所住而生其心
譬如有人身如須彌山王
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? When the Lord Buddha, in a previous life, was a disciple of Dipankara Buddha, was there communicated to him any prescribed Law, or system of doctrine, whereby he eventually became a Buddha?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! When the Lord Buddha was a disciple of Dipankara Buddha, neither prescribed Law nor system of doctrine was communicated to him, whereby he eventually became a Buddha.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? may an enlightened disciple thus ponder within himself, ‘I shall create numerous Buddhist Kingdoms’?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, kingdoms thus created would not in reality be Buddhist kingdoms, therefore ‘the creation of numerous Buddhist kingdoms’ is merely a figure of speech.” The Lord Buddha, continuing, addressed Subhuti, saying: “Enlightened disciples ought therefore to engender within themselves a pure and holy mind; they ought not to depend on the phenomena of form, sound, odour, taste, touch, or Law; they ought to sedulously cultivate a mind independent of every material aid.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “Supposing a man with a body as pretentious as Sumeru, prince among mountains, would you esteem such a body as being great?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Exceedingly great, Honoured of the Worlds! And why? Because, the Lord Buddha referred not to a physical body, but to mental and spiritual concepts of bodies, in which sense a body may be regarded as really Great.”

en.plain: You cannot stop turning over the thing your manager said on Tuesday, and it is now Saturday.
en.story:
Did the Buddha receive anything from his own teacher long ago? Nothing. Does a bodhisattva adorn buddha-lands? No; adornment is not adornment. So a bodhisattva should give rise to a pure mind that dwells nowhere: not on form, not on sound, smell, taste, touch or idea. A mind should arise that dwells on nothing.

This is the section that woke Huineng when he heard it read in a market. A remark from Tuesday still turning on Saturday has become a place the mind has settled. The remark was real and may have been unfair; the section does not argue with that. It points at the settling. A mind that arises fresh can hear the remark, decide whether it needs an answer, give the answer on Monday, and then be somewhere else. It is the difference between a bird that lands on a branch and a bird that builds a nest there.
en.reminder: Land on the branch; do not build the nest.
en.acting: Decide whether the remark needs an answer, write the answer if so, and send it on the right day.

zh_hant.plain: 主管星期二說的那句話，你到現在還在翻，而今天已經是星期六。
zh_hant.story:
佛從前有沒有從他的老師那裡得到什麼？沒有。菩薩有沒有莊嚴佛土？沒有；莊嚴不是莊嚴。所以菩薩應該生起清淨的心，無所住：不住色，不住聲、香、味、觸、法。應該無所住而生其心。

這是惠能在市集聽人誦讀時被喚醒的那一分。星期二的一句話到星期六還在翻，是因為它變成了心停下來的地方。那句話是真的，也許不公平；這一分沒有跟這件事爭。它指的是「停」。一顆新生起的心可以聽見那句話，決定它需不需要回答，星期一給出回答，然後在別的地方。這是停在樹枝上的鳥和在樹枝上築巢的鳥的差別。
zh_hant.reminder: 停在樹枝上；不要築巢。
zh_hant.acting: 決定那句話需不需要回應，需要就寫下來，在對的日子送出。

zh_hans.plain: 主管星期二说的那句话，你到现在还在翻，而今天已经是星期六。
zh_hans.story:
佛从前有没有从他的老师那里得到什么？没有。菩萨有没有庄严佛土？没有；庄严不是庄严。所以菩萨应该生起清净的心，无所住：不住色，不住声、香、味、触、法。应该无所住而生其心。

这是惠能在市集听人诵读时被唤醒的那一分。星期二的一句话到星期六还在翻，是因为它变成了心停下来的地方。那句话是真的，也许不公平；这一分没有跟这件事争。它指的是「停」。一颗新生起的心可以听见那句话，决定它需不需要回答，星期一给出回答，然后在别的地方。这是停在树枝上的鸟和在树枝上筑巢的鸟的差别。
zh_hans.reminder: 停在树枝上；不要筑巢。
zh_hans.acting: 决定那句话需不需要回应，需要就写下来，在对的日子送出。

lines: 如是沙等恆河於意云何
但諸恆河尚多無數何況其沙
我今實言告汝若有善男子
以七寶滿爾所恆河沙數三千
大千世界以用布施得福多不
佛告須菩提若善男子善女人
於此經中乃至受持四句偈等
為他人說而此福德勝前福德
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “If there were rivers Ganges as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, would the aggregate grains of sand be of considerable number?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Of very considerable number, Honoured of the Worlds! The rivers Ganges alone would be innumerable, and much more innumerable would be the grains of sand.” The Lord Buddha thereupon addressed Subhuti, saying: “I have a truth to declare unto you! If a good disciple, whether man or woman, were to bestow in the exercise of charity, an abundance of the seven treasures, sufficient to fill as many boundless universes as there would be grains of sand in these innumerable rivers, would the cumulative merit of such a disciple be considerable?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Very considerable, Honoured of the Worlds!” The Lord Buddha then declared unto Subhuti, “If a good disciple, whether man or woman, were with implicit faith to adhere to a stanza of this Scripture, and diligently explain it to others, the consequent merit would be relatively greater than the other.”

en.plain: You measure your worth in numbers, savings, followers, salary, and the numbers never feel big enough.
en.story:
If there were as many Ganges rivers as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, and a person filled that many worlds with treasure and gave it away, would the merit be great? Very great. And yet a person who keeps four lines of this teaching and explains it has merit greater than that.

The section piles number on number, sand on sand, rivers on rivers, and then sets four lines above the whole heap. It is the sutra's way of saying that numbers do not reach the thing that matters. A person measuring worth in savings and followers is standing in the heap of sand, and the heap does not add up to enough because it is not the kind of thing that adds up to enough. The four lines are the other kind. They are worth something whole, once, regardless of count.
en.reminder: Sand on sand does not add up to enough; four lines do.
en.acting: Look at one number you use to measure yourself, and put it away for the rest of the day.

zh_hant.plain: 你用數字衡量自己的價值，存款、追蹤者、薪水，數字從來不夠大。
zh_hant.story:
如果有恆河沙那麼多條恆河，一個人用珍寶裝滿那麼多世界，全部布施出去，福德多不多？很多。而一個人受持這部經的四句並解說它，福德更多過那些。

這一分把數字疊在數字上，沙疊在沙上，河疊在河上，然後把四句話放在整堆之上。這是經在說：數字到不了要緊的那樣東西。用存款和追蹤者衡量價值的人，站在那堆沙裡，而那堆沙加不到夠，因為它不是那種會加到夠的東西。四句話是另一種。它們值一個完整的東西，一次，不論數目。
zh_hant.reminder: 沙疊在沙上加不到夠；四句話夠。
zh_hant.acting: 看一個你用來衡量自己的數字，把它收起來，今天不再看。

zh_hans.plain: 你用数字衡量自己的价值，存款、追踪者、薪水，数字从来不够大。
zh_hans.story:
如果有恒河沙那么多条恒河，一个人用珍宝装满那么多世界，全部布施出去，福德多不多？很多。而一个人受持这部经的四句并解说它，福德更多过那些。

这一分把数字叠在数字上，沙叠在沙上，河叠在河上，然后把四句话放在整堆之上。这是经在说：数字到不了要紧的那样东西。用存款和追踪者衡量价值的人，站在那堆沙里，而那堆沙加不到够，因为它不是那种会加到够的东西。四句话是另一种。它们值一个完整的东西，一次，不论数目。
zh_hans.reminder: 沙叠在沙上加不到够；四句话够。
zh_hans.acting: 看一个你用来衡量自己的数字，把它收起来，今天不再看。

lines: 隨說是經乃至四句偈等
當知此處一切世間天人
阿修羅皆應供養如佛塔廟
何況有人盡能受持讀誦
當知是人成就最上第一希有
之法若是經典所在之處
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha, continuing, said unto Subhuti: “Wherever this Scripture is proclaimed, even though it were but a stanza comprising four lines, you should realise that that place would be sanctified by the presence of the whole realm of gods, men, and terrestrial spirits, who ought unitedly to worship, as if before a sacred shrine of Buddha. But what encomium shall express the merit of a disciple who rigorously observes, and diligently studies, the text of this Scripture? Subhuti, you should realise that such a disciple will be endowed with spiritual powers commensurate with initiation in the supreme, incomparable, and most wonderful Law. Whatever place constitutes a repository for this sacred Scripture, there also the Lord Buddha may be found, together with disciples worthy of reverence and honour.”

en.plain: Your desk, your kitchen table, your bus seat: none of it feels like a place where anything worthwhile could happen.
en.story:
Wherever even four lines of this teaching are spoken, that place should be honoured by every kind of being as if it were a shrine; how much more the place where the whole teaching is kept. Wherever the teaching is, there the Buddha is, and the honoured disciples.

The section makes a place holy by what is said in it, not by what it is. A bus seat where four lines are read is, for the length of the reading, a shrine. The kitchen table where the line is copied is the place the section is talking about. This is not a metaphor the sutra is being generous with; it is the sutra's plain claim about where the important thing happens, which is wherever someone lets it. The desk is not too small for it.
en.reminder: Wherever the line is read, that is the place.
en.acting: Read today's line aloud, once, wherever you happen to be sitting, and let that be the shrine.

zh_hant.plain: 你的書桌、廚房餐桌、公車座位：沒有一個像是能發生任何有價值的事的地方。
zh_hant.story:
凡是說了這部經哪怕四句的地方，一切天人都應該像對塔廟那樣供養；何況有人能完整受持這部經的地方。經在哪裡，佛就在哪裡，尊貴的弟子也在。

這一分靠在一個地方說了什麼，讓那個地方變神聖，而不是靠那個地方是什麼。一個讀了四句的公車座位，在讀的那段時間裡，是塔廟。抄這一句的廚房餐桌，就是這一分在說的地方。這不是經在慷慨地使用比喻；這是經對「要緊的事在哪裡發生」的平實說法，那就是任何人讓它發生的地方。書桌不會小到裝不下它。
zh_hant.reminder: 這一句在哪裡被讀，哪裡就是那個地方。
zh_hant.acting: 今天把這一句大聲讀一次，就在你剛好坐著的地方，讓那裡成為塔廟。

zh_hans.plain: 你的书桌、厨房餐桌、公车座位：没有一个像是能发生任何有价值的事的地方。
zh_hans.story:
凡是说了这部经哪怕四句的地方，一切天人都应该像对塔庙那样供养；何况有人能完整受持这部经的地方。经在哪里，佛就在哪里，尊贵的弟子也在。

这一分靠在一个地方说了什么，让那个地方变神圣，而不是靠那个地方是什么。一个读了四句的公车座位，在读的那段时间里，是塔庙。抄这一句的厨房餐桌，就是这一分在说的地方。这不是经在慷慨地使用比喻；这是经对「要紧的事在哪里发生」的平实说法，那就是任何人让它发生的地方。书桌不会小到装不下它。
zh_hans.reminder: 这一句在哪里被读，哪里就是那个地方。
zh_hans.acting: 今天把这一句大声读一次，就在你刚好坐着的地方，让那里成为塔庙。

lines: 爾時須菩提白佛言世尊
是經名為金剛般若波羅蜜
三千大千世界所有微塵
如來說世界非世界是名世界
可以三十二相見如來不
不可以三十二相得見如來
如來說三十二相即是非相
乃至受持四句偈等為他人說
chapters.translation_en: Upon that occasion, Subhuti enquired of the Lord Buddha, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! by what name shall this Scripture be known, that we may regard it with reverence?” The Lord Buddha replied, saying: “Subhuti, this Scripture shall be known as _The Diamond Sutra_, ‘The Transcendent Wisdom,’ by means of which we reach ‘The Other Shore.’ By this name you shall reverently regard it! And why? Subhuti, what the Lord Buddha declared as ‘transcendent wisdom’ by means of which we reach ‘the other shore,’ is not essentially ‘transcendent wisdom’—in its essence it transcends all wisdom.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Did the Lord Buddha formulate a precise system of Law or doctrine?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! The Lord Buddha did not formulate a precise system of Law or doctrine.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? within the myriad worlds which comprise this universe, are the atoms of dust numerous?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Very numerous, Honoured of the Worlds!” The Lord Buddha continuing his discourse, said: “Subhuti, the Lord Buddha declares that all these ‘atoms of dust’ are not essentially ‘atoms of dust,’ they are merely termed ‘atoms of dust.’ The Lord Buddha also declares that those ‘myriad worlds’ are not really ‘myriad worlds,’ they are merely designated ‘myriad worlds.’” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Can the Lord Buddha be perceived by means of his thirty-two bodily distinctions?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha cannot be perceived by means of his thirty-two bodily distinctions. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha referred to as his ‘thirty-two bodily distinctions,’ are not in reality ‘bodily distinctions,’ they are merely defined as ‘bodily distinctions.’” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “If a good disciple, whether man or woman, day by day sacrificed lives innumerable as the sands of the Ganges; and if another disciple adhered with implicit faith to a stanza of this Scripture, and diligently explained it to others, the intrinsic merit of such a disciple would be relatively greater than the other.”

en.plain: Someone asked you what you actually believe, or what this practice is for, and you had no name for it.
en.story:
Subhuti asks what the teaching should be called. The Buddha names it: the Diamond of Perfect Wisdom; and adds at once that what is called perfect wisdom is not perfect wisdom. Has the Buddha taught anything? Nothing. Are the dust particles of the world many? Many, and not dust. Can the Buddha be seen by his marks? No. And again: keeping four lines outweighs giving away lives as many as the Ganges sands.

The section gives the teaching a name and takes it back in the same breath. That is not evasiveness; it is what the practice is like from inside. Asked what it is for, the honest answer is a plain description: I copy one line a day, I read what it means, I breathe. The name is not the thing. The doing is the thing, and it does not need to be defended by a name.
en.reminder: The name is not the thing; the doing is.
en.acting: When asked what the practice is, describe what you do in one plain sentence and stop there.

zh_hant.plain: 有人問你到底相信什麼，或這個練習是為了什麼，你說不出一個名字。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提問這部經該叫什麼。佛給了名字：金剛般若波羅蜜；同一口氣又說，所謂般若波羅蜜，不是般若波羅蜜。佛有沒有說法？沒有。世界的微塵多不多？多，而且不是微塵。能不能靠相見佛？不能。再一次：受持四句，勝過布施恆河沙那麼多的身命。

這一分給了教法一個名字，又在同一口氣裡收回。那不是迴避；那是修行從裡面看起來的樣子。被問到它是為了什麼，誠實的回答是一段平實的描述：我一天抄一句，讀它的意思，呼吸。名字不是那樣東西。做，才是，而做不需要靠一個名字來辯護。
zh_hant.reminder: 名字不是那樣東西；做才是。
zh_hant.acting: 被問到這個練習是什麼時，用一句平常的話描述你做什麼，然後停在那裡。

zh_hans.plain: 有人问你到底相信什么，或这个练习是为了什么，你说不出一个名字。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提问这部经该叫什么。佛给了名字：金刚般若波罗蜜；同一口气又说，所谓般若波罗蜜，不是般若波罗蜜。佛有没有说法？没有。世界的微尘多不多？多，而且不是微尘。能不能靠相见佛？不能。再一次：受持四句，胜过布施恒河沙那么多的身命。

这一分给了教法一个名字，又在同一口气里收回。那不是回避；那是修行从里面看起来的样子。被问到它是为了什么，诚实的回答是一段平实的描述：我一天抄一句，读它的意思，呼吸。名字不是那样东西。做，才是，而做不需要靠一个名字来辩护。
zh_hans.reminder: 名字不是那样东西；做才是。
zh_hans.acting: 被问到这个练习是什么时，用一句平常的话描述你做什么，然后停在那里。

lines: 深解義趣涕淚悲泣而白佛言
若復有人得聞是經信心清淨
我今得聞如是經典信解受持
若當來世後五百歲其有眾生
此人無我相無人相無眾生相
人相眾生相壽者相即是非相
若復有人得聞是經不驚不怖
不畏當知是人甚為希有
如我昔為歌利王割截身體
我於爾時無我相無人相
若有我相人相眾生相壽者相
作忍辱仙人於爾所世無我相
無人相無眾生相無壽者相
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心
不應住色生心不應住聲香味
觸法生心應生無所住心
菩薩為利益一切眾生故
如來說一切諸相即是非相
又說一切眾生即非眾生
如來是真語者實語者如語者
如來所得法此法無實無虛
若菩薩心住於法而行布施
若菩薩心不住法而行布施
如人有目日光明照見種種色
當來之世若有善男子善女人
能於此經受持讀誦則為如來
皆得成就無量無邊功德
chapters.translation_en: Upon that occasion, the venerable Subhuti, hearing the text of this scripture proclaimed, and profoundly realising its meaning, was moved to tears. Addressing the Lord Buddha, he said: “Thou art of transcendent wisdom, Honoured of the Worlds! The Lord Buddha in expounding this supreme canon of Scripture, surpassed in perspicuity every exposition previously heard by me, since my eyes were privileged to perceive this most excellent wisdom. Honoured of the Worlds! In years to come, if disciples hearing this scripture proclaimed, and having within their minds a pure and holy faith, engender true concepts of the ephemeral nature of phenomena—we ought to realise that the cumulative merit of such disciples will be intrinsic and wonderful. Honoured of the Worlds! The true concept of phenomena is, that these are not essentially phenomena, and hence the Lord Buddha declared that they are merely termed phenomena.” “Honoured of the Worlds! having heard this unprecedented Scripture, faith, clear understanding, and firm resolve to observe its precepts, follow as a natural sequence. If, in future ages, disciples destined to hear this Scripture, likewise believe, understand, and observe its precepts, their merit will incite the highest wonder and praise. And why? Because, the minds of those disciples will have outgrown such arbitrary ideas of phenomena as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality. And why? Because, the entity is in reality non-entity; and a being, a living being, or a personality, are ideas equally nebulous and hypothetical. Wherefore, discarding every arbitrary idea of phenomena, the wise and wholly enlightened were severally designated Buddha.” The Lord Buddha, assenting, said unto Subhuti: “If, in future ages, disciples destined to hear this Scripture, neither become perturbed by its extreme modes of thought, nor alarmed by its lofty sentiments, nor apprehensive about realising its high ideals—these disciples also, by their intrinsic merit, will incite superlative wonder and praise.” “Subhuti, what the Lord Buddha referred to as the first _Paramita_ (charity), is not in reality the first _Paramita_, it is merely termed the first _Paramita_” “Subhuti, regarding the third _Paramita_ (endurance), it is not in reality a _Paramita_, it is merely termed a _Paramita_. And why? Because, in a previous life, when the Prince of Kalinga (‘Kaliradja’) severed the flesh from my limbs and body, at that time I was oblivious to such arbitrary ideas of phenomena as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality. And why? Because, upon that occasion, when my limbs and body were rent asunder, had I not been oblivious to such arbitrary ideas as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality, there would have originated within my mind, feelings of anger and resentment.” “Subhuti, five hundred incarnations ago, I recollect that as a recluse practising the ordinances of the Kshanti-Paramita, even then I had no such arbitrary ideas as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality. Therefore, Subhuti, an enlightened disciple ought to discard as being unreal and illusive, every conceivable form of phenomena. In aspiring to supreme spiritual wisdom, the mind ought to be insensible to every sensuous influence, and independent of everything pertaining to sound, odour, taste, touch, or Law. There ought to be cultivated a condition of complete independence of mind; because, if the mind is depending upon any external aid, it is obviously deluded—there is in reality nothing external to depend upon. Therefore, the Lord Buddha declared that in the exercise of charity, the mind of an enlightened disciple ought not to depend upon any form of phenomena. Subhuti, an enlightened disciple desirous to confer benefits upon the whole realm of being, ought thus to be animated in the exercise of charity.” The Lord Buddha, in declaring the “unreality of phenomena,” also affirmed “that the whole realm of sentient life is ephemeral and illusory.” “Subhuti, the sayings of the Lord Buddha are true, credible, and immutable. His utterances are neither extravagant nor chimerical. Subhuti, the plane of thought to which the Lord Buddha attained, cannot be explained in terms synonymous with reality or non-reality.” “Subhuti, in the exercise of charity, if the mind of an enlightened disciple is not independent of every Law, he is like unto a person having entered impenetrable darkness, and to whom every object is invisible. But an enlightened disciple, discharging the exercise of charity with a mind independent of every Law, is like unto a person having the power of vision, in the meridian glory of the sunlight, and to whom every object is visible.” “Subhuti, in future ages, if a good disciple, whether man or woman, rigorously studies and observes the text of this Scripture; the Lord Buddha, by means of his Buddhic wisdom, entirely knows and perceives that for such a disciple there is reserved a cumulative merit, immeasurable and illimitable.”

en.plain: Something was done to you that was unfair, and every time you remember it the anger comes back whole.
en.story:
Subhuti weeps at the teaching. The Buddha then tells of a former life in which a king cut his body apart limb by limb, and says that at that time he held no idea of a self, a person, a being, a life; had he held one, he would have felt hatred. The perfection of patience, he says, is not the perfection of patience. A bodhisattva should give rise to a mind that dwells nowhere, and the Buddha's words are true, real, and neither true nor false.

The story of the king is the sutra's hardest example of patience, and it is not asking anyone to be cut apart without anger. It is describing what the anger is made of: a self that was wronged, held so that the wrong can be replayed. The wrong was real; the section does not say otherwise. It says the whole-returning anger needs a self to return to, and that the self can be held a little less tightly. Not forgiveness, which is a separate matter. Just less grip.
en.reminder: The anger returns to a self; hold the self less tightly.
en.acting: Next time the memory comes, name it once, 'that happened', and then do the next ordinary thing.

zh_hant.plain: 有人對你做了不公平的事，每次想起來，怒氣就完整地回來。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提聽法流淚。佛接著說一個前世：一個王把他的身體一節一節割開，而他那時沒有我相、人相、眾生相、壽者相；如果有，他會生恨。他說，忍辱波羅蜜，不是忍辱波羅蜜。菩薩應該生起無所住的心，而佛的話是真的、實的，不真也不假。

那個王的故事是這部經關於忍最難的例子，它不是要任何人被割開而不生氣。它描述的是怒氣是什麼做的：一個被虧待的自己，被抓著，好讓那件虧待可以重播。虧待是真的；這一分沒有說不是。它說完整回來的怒氣需要一個可以回去的自己，而那個自己可以抓得鬆一點。不是原諒，那是另一件事。只是少一點抓。
zh_hant.reminder: 怒氣回到一個自己；把那個自己抓鬆一點。
zh_hant.acting: 下次記憶來的時候，叫它一次「那件事發生過」，然後做下一件平常的事。

zh_hans.plain: 有人对你做了不公平的事，每次想起来，怒气就完整地回来。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提听法流泪。佛接着说一个前世：一个王把他的身体一节一节割开，而他那时没有我相、人相、众生相、寿者相；如果有，他会生恨。他说，忍辱波罗蜜，不是忍辱波罗蜜。菩萨应该生起无所住的心，而佛的话是真的、实的，不真也不假。

那个王的故事是这部经关于忍最难的例子，它不是要任何人被割开而不生气。它描述的是怒气是什么做的：一个被亏待的自己，被抓着，好让那件亏待可以重播。亏待是真的；这一分没有说不是。它说完整回来的怒气需要一个可以回去的自己，而那个自己可以抓得松一点。不是原谅，那是另一件事。只是少一点抓。
zh_hans.reminder: 怒气回到一个自己；把那个自己抓松一点。
zh_hans.acting: 下次记忆来的时候，叫它一次「那件事发生过」，然后做下一件平常的事。

lines: 初日分以恆河沙等身布施
中日分復以恆河沙等身布施
後日分亦以恆河沙等身布施
若復有人聞此經典信心不逆
其福勝彼何況書寫受持讀誦
以要言之是經有不可思議
若有人能受持讀誦廣為人說
如來悉知是人悉見是人
皆得成就不可量不可稱
則為荷擔如來阿耨多羅三藐
若樂小法者著我見人見
則於此經不能聽受讀誦
在在處處若有此經一切世間
當知此處則為是塔皆應恭敬
作禮圍遶以諸華香而散其處
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “If a good disciple, whether man or woman, in the morning, at noonday, and at eventide, sacrificed lives innumerable as the sands of the Ganges, and thus without intermission throughout infinite ages; and if another disciple, hearing this Scripture proclaimed, steadfastly believed it, his felicity would be appreciably greater than the other. But how much greater must be the felicity of a disciple who transcribes the sacred text, observes its precepts, studies its Laws, and repeats the Scripture that others may be edified thereby?” “Subhuti, the relative importance of this Scripture may thus be summarily stated: its truth is infinite; its worth incomparable; and its merit interminable.” “The Lord Buddha delivered this Scripture specifically for those who are entered upon the path which leads to Nirvana, and for those who are attaining to the ultimate plane of Buddhic thought. If a disciple rigorously observes, studies, and widely disseminates the knowledge of this Scripture, the Lord Buddha entirely knows and perceives that for such an one there will be a cumulative merit, immeasurable, incomparable, illimitable, and inconceivable. All such disciples will be endowed with transcendent Buddhic wisdom and enlightenment. And why? Because, Subhuti, if a disciple takes pleasure in a narrow or exclusive form of the Law, he cannot receive with gratification the instruction of this Scripture, or delight in its study, or fervently explain it to others. Subhuti, in whatever place there is a repository for this Scripture, the whole realm of spiritual beings ought to adore it; and reverencing it as a sacred shrine, ceremoniously surround it, scattering profusely sweet-scented flowers, and pure odours of fragrant incense.”

en.plain: You keep starting things, courses, habits, projects, and dropping them, and you have begun to think you are simply someone who does not finish.
en.story:
If a person gave away their life three times a day for countless ages, and another simply heard this teaching and did not turn from it, the second's merit would be greater; how much more to write, keep, read and explain it. This teaching is for those who set out on the great way; those who cling to a self cannot hear it. Wherever it is kept, that place is a shrine.

The section's bar is low on purpose: to hear the teaching and not turn away. Not to master it, finish it, or keep a perfect record. For a person who starts and drops things, this is the encouraging measure. The practice is not a course to complete. It is a line a day, and the days that were missed are not counted anywhere. Not turning away is enough, and it can be resumed at any line.
en.reminder: Not turning away is enough; it can be resumed at any line.
en.acting: Resume one dropped thing today at the smallest possible size, and let that count as not turning away.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直開始新的東西，課程、習慣、計畫，然後放掉，你開始覺得自己就是一個做不完事情的人。
zh_hant.story:
如果一個人在無數劫裡每天三次捨身布施，而另一個人只是聽到這部經，沒有轉身離開，第二個人的福德更大；何況書寫、受持、讀誦、解說。這部經是為發大乘心的人說的；執著一個我的人聽不進去。經在哪裡，哪裡就是塔。

這一分的門檻故意放低：聽到教法，不轉身離開。不是精通它，完成它，或保持完美的紀錄。對一個開始又放掉的人，這是一種鼓勵的量法。這個練習不是一門要完成的課。它是一天一句，而漏掉的日子沒有被記在任何地方。不轉身離開就夠了，而且從任何一句都可以接下去。
zh_hant.reminder: 不轉身離開就夠了；從任何一句都可以接下去。
zh_hant.acting: 今天用最小的尺寸重新接上一件放掉的事，讓它算作沒有轉身離開。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直开始新的东西，课程、习惯、计划，然后放掉，你开始觉得自己就是一个做不完事情的人。
zh_hans.story:
如果一个人在无数劫里每天三次舍身布施，而另一个人只是听到这部经，没有转身离开，第二个人的福德更大；何况书写、受持、读诵、解说。这部经是为发大乘心的人说的；执着一个我的人听不进去。经在哪里，哪里就是塔。

这一分的门槛故意放低：听到教法，不转身离开。不是精通它，完成它，或保持完美的纪录。对一个开始又放掉的人，这是一种鼓励的量法。这个练习不是一门要完成的课。它是一天一句，而漏掉的日子没有被记在任何地方。不转身离开就够了，而且从任何一句都可以接下去。
zh_hans.reminder: 不转身离开就够了；从任何一句都可以接下去。
zh_hans.acting: 今天用最小的尺寸重新接上一件放掉的事，让它算作没有转身离开。

lines: 善男子善女人受持讀誦此經
若為人輕賤是人先世罪業
當得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
我念過去無量阿僧祇劫
得值八百四千萬億那由他諸
佛悉皆供養承事無空過者
能受持讀誦此經所得功德
乃至算數譬喻所不能及
若善男子善女人於後末世
或有人聞心則狂亂狐疑不信
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha, continuing, addressed Subhuti, saying: “If a good disciple, whether man or woman, devoted to the observance and study of this Scripture, is thereby despised, or lightly esteemed, it is because that in a previous life there had been committed some grievous transgression, followed now by inexorable retribution. But, although in this life despised or lightly esteemed, the compensating merit thus acquired will cause the transgression of a former life to be fully expiated, and the disciple adequately recompensed by the attainment of supreme spiritual wisdom.” “Furthermore, Subhuti, numberless ages ago, I recollect that before the advent of Dipankara Buddha, there were myriad Buddhas before whom I served and received religious instruction, my conduct being entirely blameless and without reproach. But, in the ages to come, if a disciple be enabled to rigorously observe and to study the text of this Scripture, the merit thus acquired will so far exceed the measure of my merit in the service of those myriad Buddhas, that it cannot be stated in terms of proportion, nor comprehended by means of any ‘analogy.’” “Again, Subhuti, in future ages, if a good disciple, whether man or woman, be enabled to rigorously observe and to study consecutively the texts of this Scripture, were I to elaborate either the nature or extent of this merit, those who heard it might become delirious, or entirely doubt its credibility. Subhuti, it is necessary to realise, that as the meaning of this Scripture is beyond ordinary comprehension, the scope of its fruitful rewards is equally incomprehensible.”

en.plain: You are being punished, socially or at work, for something small, and it feels out of all proportion.
en.story:
If a person who keeps this teaching is despised by others, it is because the wrongs of former lives would have led to a worse fate; through being despised now, those wrongs are cleared. The Buddha then says that the merit of keeping the teaching in a later age is beyond anything he could describe, and that some hearing it would go mad; the meaning of the teaching cannot be conceived, and neither can its fruit.

The section reads a small present humiliation as the clearing of a larger debt, and whatever one thinks of the accounting, the effect on the person humiliated is practical: the small punishment is the small punishment, not the beginning of a fall. It is out of proportion because proportion was never the point; something is being paid off cheaply. Take the small hit. Do not add the larger story to it.
en.reminder: Take the small hit; do not add the larger story.
en.acting: Write down exactly what the punishment was, in one plain line, and read it back at its real size.

zh_hant.plain: 你因為一件小事在社交上或公司裡被懲罰，感覺完全不成比例。
zh_hant.story:
如果受持這部經的人被別人輕賤，那是因為前世的罪業本來會導向更糟的結果；因為現在被輕賤，那些罪業就消掉了。佛接著說，後世受持這部經的福德，超過他所能描述的，有人聽了會狂亂；這部經的義理不可思議，它的果報也不可思議。

這一分把眼前小小的屈辱讀成一筆更大的債的清償，不論你怎麼看這種記帳，它對被屈辱的人的作用是實際的：小懲罰就是小懲罰，不是一場跌落的開始。它不成比例，是因為比例從來就不是重點；有什麼東西正在被便宜地付清。接下這個小打擊。不要把更大的故事加上去。
zh_hant.reminder: 接下小打擊；不要把更大的故事加上去。
zh_hant.acting: 用一行平實的話寫下懲罰到底是什麼，然後用它真正的大小讀回來。

zh_hans.plain: 你因为一件小事在社交上或公司里被惩罚，感觉完全不成比例。
zh_hans.story:
如果受持这部经的人被别人轻贱，那是因为前世的罪业本来会导向更糟的结果；因为现在被轻贱，那些罪业就消掉了。佛接着说，后世受持这部经的福德，超过他所能描述的，有人听了会狂乱；这部经的义理不可思议，它的果报也不可思议。

这一分把眼前小小的屈辱读成一笔更大的债的清偿，不论你怎么看这种记帐，它对被屈辱的人的作用是实际的：小惩罚就是小惩罚，不是一场跌落的开始。它不成比例，是因为比例从来就不是重点；有什么东西正在被便宜地付清。接下这个小打击。不要把更大的故事加上去。
zh_hans.reminder: 接下小打击；不要把更大的故事加上去。
zh_hans.acting: 用一行平实的话写下惩罚到底是什么，然后用它真正的大小读回来。

lines: 爾時須菩提白佛言世尊
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心
佛告須菩提善男子善女人
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者
而無有一眾生實滅度者
若菩薩有我相人相眾生相
發阿耨多羅三藐三菩提心者
有法得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
無有法得阿耨多羅三藐三菩
如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
者燃燈佛則不與我授記
以實無有法得阿耨多羅三藐
是故燃燈佛與我授記作是言
如來得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
佛得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
如來所得阿耨多羅三藐三菩
是故如來說一切法皆是佛法
所言一切法者即非一切法
如來說人身長大則為非大身
若作是言我當滅度無量眾生
是故佛說一切法無我無人
若菩薩作是言我當莊嚴佛土
如來說莊嚴佛土者即非莊嚴
chapters.translation_en: Upon that occasion, the venerable Subhuti addressed the Lord Buddha, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! if a good disciple, whether man or woman, having desired to attain to supreme spiritual wisdom, what immutable Law shall support the mind of that disciple, and bring into subjection every inordinate desire?” The Lord Buddha replied, saying: “A good disciple, whether man or woman, ought thus to habituate his mind: ‘I must become oblivious to every idea of sentient life; and having become oblivious to every idea of sentient life, there is _no one_ to whom the idea of sentient life has become oblivious.’ And why? Because, Subhuti, if an enlightened disciple retains within his mind such arbitrary ideas of sentient life as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality, he has not attained to supreme spiritual wisdom. And why? Because, Subhuti, there is no Law by means of which a disciple may be defined as one having obtained supreme spiritual wisdom.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? When the Lord Buddha was a disciple of Dipankara Buddha, was there bequeathed to him any Law whereby he attained to supreme spiritual wisdom?” Subhuti replied, saying: “No! Honoured of the Worlds! inasmuch as I am able to comprehend the meaning of the Lord Buddha’s discourse, when the Lord Buddha was a disciple of Dipankara Buddha, there was no Law bequeathed to him whereby he attained to supreme spiritual wisdom.” The Lord Buddha endorsed these words, saying: “Truly there is no Law by means of which the Lord Buddha obtained supreme spiritual wisdom. Subhuti, if there existed a Law by means of which the Lord Buddha obtained supreme spiritual wisdom, Dipankara Buddha would not have foretold at my initiation, ‘In future ages thou shalt become Sakyamuni Buddha.’ But, in reality, there is no Law by means of which supreme spiritual wisdom can be obtained. Therefore, at my initiation, Dipankara Buddha foretold concerning me, ‘In future ages, thou shalt become Sakyamuni Buddha.’ And why? Because, in the word _Buddha_. every Law is summarily and intelligibly comprehended.” “If a disciple affirmed that the Lord Buddha attained to supreme spiritual wisdom, it is necessary to state that there is no Law whereby this condition of mind can be realised. The supreme spiritual wisdom to which the Lord Buddha attained, cannot, in its essence, be defined as real or unreal. Thus, the Lord Buddha declared that the ordinarily accepted term, ‘the Buddhic Law,’ is synonymous with every moral and spiritual Law. Subhuti, what are ordinarily declared to be ‘systems of Law,’ are not in reality ‘systems of Law,’ they are merely termed ‘systems of Law.’” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “Can you imagine a man having a great physical body?” Subhuti replied, saying: “The Lord Buddha, discoursing upon the proportions of a physical body, did not maintain for these any _real_ greatness, therefore it is merely termed ‘a great body.”’ The Lord Buddha, thereupon, addressed Subhuti, saying: “Thus it is with an enlightened disciple: if he were to expatiate after this manner, ‘I must become oblivious to every idea of sentient life,’ he could not be described as fully enlightened. And why? Because, there is no Law whereby a disciple can be approved as ‘fully enlightened.’ Therefore, the Lord Buddha declared that within the realm of spiritual Law, there is neither an entity, a being, a living being, nor a personality.” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “If an enlightened disciple were to speak in this wise, ‘I shall create numerous Buddhist kingdoms,’ he could not be designated ‘fully enlightened.’ And why? Because, the Lord Buddha, discoursing upon ‘creating numerous Buddhist kingdoms,’ did not affirm the idea of creating numerous ‘material’ Buddhist kingdoms, hence the ‘creation of numerous Buddhist kingdoms’ is merely a figure of speech. Subhuti, the Lord Buddha declared that a disciple may be regarded as ‘truly enlightened,’ whose mind is thoroughly imbued with the Law of non-individuality.”

en.plain: You keep asking yourself who you really are, the job, the roles, the labels, and no answer holds.
en.story:
Subhuti asks the opening question again, and the Buddha answers it again from the other side: a bodhisattva liberates all beings and yet no being is liberated, because a bodhisattva with a self is not a bodhisattva. Then: was there anything the Buddha attained? Nothing; that is why it is called attainment. All things are Buddha-things, and all things are not things. A person who says 'I will liberate beings' is not a bodhisattva; a person who sees no self in things is.

The section circles the question of identity and refuses to hand back a label. The answer that holds is that none holds, and the sutra treats that as good news rather than a loss. The roles are real and can be done well; the labels are not what does them. You are the doing, and the doing does not need a name to go on.
en.reminder: No label holds; the doing does not need one.
en.acting: Spend one day without describing yourself to anyone, and notice how much still gets done.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直問自己到底是誰，工作、角色、標籤，沒有一個答案站得住。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提再問一次開頭的問題，佛從另一邊再答一次：菩薩度一切眾生，而沒有一個眾生被度，因為有我的菩薩不是菩薩。然後：佛有沒有得到什麼？沒有；所以才叫得到。一切法都是佛法，一切法都不是法。說「我要度眾生」的人不是菩薩；看見法裡沒有我的人才是。

這一分繞著身分的問題，拒絕交回一個標籤。站得住的答案是沒有一個站得住，而經把這當好消息，不當損失。角色是真的，可以做得好；標籤不是做它們的東西。你是那個做，而做不需要一個名字才能繼續。
zh_hant.reminder: 沒有一個標籤站得住；做，不需要標籤。
zh_hant.acting: 一天不向任何人描述自己，注意有多少事照樣做完了。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直问自己到底是谁，工作、角色、标签，没有一个答案站得住。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提再问一次开头的问题，佛从另一边再答一次：菩萨度一切众生，而没有一个众生被度，因为有我的菩萨不是菩萨。然后：佛有没有得到什么？没有；所以才叫得到。一切法都是佛法，一切法都不是法。说「我要度众生」的人不是菩萨；看见法里没有我的人才是。

这一分绕着身分的问题，拒绝交回一个标签。站得住的答案是没有一个站得住，而经把这当好消息，不当损失。角色是真的，可以做得好；标签不是做它们的东西。你是那个做，而做不需要一个名字才能继续。
zh_hans.reminder: 没有一个标签站得住；做，不需要标签。
zh_hans.acting: 一天不向任何人描述自己，注意有多少事照样做完了。

lines: 如恆河中所有沙佛說是沙不
佛告須菩提爾所國土中
所有眾生若干種心如來悉知
過去心不可得現在心不可得
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Does the Lord Buddha possess the physical eye?” Subhuti assented, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha truly possesses the physical eye.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Does the Lord Buddha possess the divine or spiritual eye?” Subhuti assented, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha truly possesses the divine or spiritual eye.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Does the Lord Buddha possess the eye of wisdom?” Subhuti assented, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha truly possesses the eye of wisdom.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Does the Lord Buddha possess the eye of truth?” Subhuti assented, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha truly possesses the eye of truth.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Does the Lord Buddha possess the Buddhic eye?” Subhuti assented, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha truly possesses the Buddhic eye.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Concerning the sands of the Ganges, did the Lord Buddha declare that these were grains of sand?” Subhuti assenting, said: “Honoured of the Worlds! the Lord Buddha declared that these were grains of sand.” The Lord Buddha enquired of Subhuti, saying: “What think you? If there were as many rivers Ganges as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, and if there were as many Buddhist worlds as the grains of sand in those innumerable rivers, would these Buddhist worlds be numerous?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! these Buddhist worlds would be very numerous.” The Lord Buddha, continuing, addressed Subhuti, saying: “Within these innumerable worlds, every form of sentient life, with their various mental dispositions, are entirely known to the Lord Buddha. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha referred to as their ‘various mental dispositions,’ are not in reality their ‘various mental dispositions,’ these are merely termed their ‘various mental dispositions.’ And why? Because, Subhuti, dispositions of mind, or modes of thought, whether relating to the past, the present, or the future, are alike unreal and illusory.”

en.plain: The decision you made two years ago, the job you turned down, the flat you sold, plays on repeat.
en.story:
Does the Buddha have the physical eye, the heavenly eye, the wisdom eye, the teaching eye, the Buddha eye? Yes to each. Does he know the minds of all the beings in all the worlds as numerous as the sands of countless Ganges rivers? Yes; and those minds are not minds, and are called minds. Why? The past mind cannot be grasped, the present mind cannot be grasped, the future mind cannot be grasped.

Regret is an attempt to hold the past mind: to stand again in the room where the decision was made and choose differently. The room is gone, and the person who chose in it had only what they knew then. That is not a consolation prize; it is simply the geometry. What can be held is the present decision, usually smaller and less dramatic than the old one: the next application, the next month's budget. The old decision closes only when the new one is made.
en.reminder: The room where you chose is gone; the next room is here.
en.acting: Make one present decision today that the old decision was blocking.

zh_hant.plain: 兩年前的那個決定，推掉的工作、賣掉的房子，一直重播。
zh_hant.story:
佛有沒有肉眼、天眼、慧眼、法眼、佛眼？每一個都有。他知不知道無數恆河沙那麼多世界裡一切眾生的心？知道；而那些心不是心，叫做心。為什麼？過去心不可得，現在心不可得，未來心不可得。

後悔是抓住過去的心的嘗試：再站進做決定的那個房間，選另一邊。那個房間已經沒有了，在裡面選的那個人只有他那時知道的東西。這不是安慰獎；這只是幾何。抓得住的是現在的決定，它通常比舊的那個小、也沒那麼戲劇：下一份申請，下一個月的預算。舊決定只在新決定做出來的時候才會關上。
zh_hant.reminder: 你選擇的那個房間沒有了；下一個房間在這裡。
zh_hant.acting: 今天做一個被舊決定擋住的、現在的決定。

zh_hans.plain: 两年前的那个决定，推掉的工作、卖掉的房子，一直重播。
zh_hans.story:
佛有没有肉眼、天眼、慧眼、法眼、佛眼？每一个都有。他知不知道无数恒河沙那么多世界里一切众生的心？知道；而那些心不是心，叫做心。为什么？过去心不可得，现在心不可得，未来心不可得。

后悔是抓住过去的心的尝试：再站进做决定的那个房间，选另一边。那个房间已经没有了，在里面选的那个人只有他那时知道的东西。这不是安慰奖；这只是几何。抓得住的是现在的决定，它通常比旧的那个小、也没那么戏剧：下一份申请，下一个月的预算。旧决定只在新决定做出来的时候才会关上。
zh_hans.reminder: 你选择的那个房间没有了；下一个房间在这里。
zh_hans.acting: 今天做一个被旧决定挡住的、现在的决定。

lines: 若有人滿三千大千世界七寶
以用布施是人以是因緣
此人以是因緣得福甚多
以福德無故如來說得福德多
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? If a disciple, having obtained all the treasures of this universe, were to bestow these in the exercise of charity, would such a disciple consequently enjoy a considerable merit?” Subhuti assenting, said: “Honoured of the Worlds! such a disciple would consequently enjoy a very considerable merit.” The Lord Buddha thereupon addressed Subhuti, saying: “If there were any real or permanent quality in merit, the Lord Buddha would not have spoken of such merit as ‘considerable.’ It is because there is neither a tangible nor material quality in merit, that the Lord Buddha referred to the merit of that disciple as ‘considerable.’”

en.plain: You did something good, and the fact that nobody noticed has soured it.
en.story:
If a person filled three thousand worlds with treasure and gave it away, would the merit be great? Yes, says Subhuti. The Buddha: if merit were real, I would not say it was great; it is because merit is not merit that I say it is great.

The section takes the good deed and removes the scoreboard. Merit that is real could be tallied and noticed and withheld; merit that is not merit cannot be soured by anyone's inattention because it was never on the board. The good thing done was the whole of it. The noticing was never part of the deed, and its absence takes nothing from the deed. What sours is the wish to have been seen, which can be set aside separately, and is lighter once it is named.
en.reminder: The deed was whole without the noticing.
en.acting: Name to yourself the wish to have been seen, then do one more good thing where no one will.

zh_hant.plain: 你做了一件好事，沒有人注意到這件事讓它變酸了。
zh_hant.story:
如果一個人用珍寶裝滿三千大千世界布施，福德多不多？多，須菩提說。佛：福德如果是真的，我就不會說它多；正因為福德不是福德，我才說它多。

這一分把好事留下，把記分板拿走。真的福德可以被計算、被注意、被扣留；不是福德的福德不會因為誰不注意而變酸，因為它從來沒有在板子上。做了的好事就是全部。被注意從來不是那件事的一部分，它的缺席不會從那件事拿走任何東西。變酸的是想被看見的願望，那可以另外放到一邊，而叫出名字之後它就輕了。
zh_hant.reminder: 那件事沒有被注意也是完整的。
zh_hant.acting: 對自己說出想被看見的願望，然後再做一件沒有人會看見的好事。

zh_hans.plain: 你做了一件好事，没有人注意到这件事让它变酸了。
zh_hans.story:
如果一个人用珍宝装满三千大千世界布施，福德多不多？多，须菩提说。佛：福德如果是真的，我就不会说它多；正因为福德不是福德，我才说它多。

这一分把好事留下，把记分板拿走。真的福德可以被计算、被注意、被扣留；不是福德的福德不会因为谁不注意而变酸，因为它从来没有在板子上。做了的好事就是全部。被注意从来不是那件事的一部分，它的缺席不会从那件事拿走任何东西。变酸的是想被看见的愿望，那可以另外放到一边，而叫出名字之后它就轻了。
zh_hans.reminder: 那件事没有被注意也是完整的。
zh_hans.acting: 对自己说出想被看见的愿望，然后再做一件没有人会看见的好事。

lines: 如來不應以具足色身見
即非具足色身是名具足色身
如來可以具足諸相見不
如來不應以具足諸相見
如來說諸相具足即非具足
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Can the Lord Buddha be perceived by means of his perfect material body?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! it is improbable that the Lord Buddha can be perceived by means of his perfect material body. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha referred to as a ‘perfect material body,’ is not in reality a ‘perfect material body,’ it is merely termed a ‘perfect material body.’” The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “What think you? Can the Lord Buddha be perceived by means of any physical phenomena?” Subhuti replied, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! it is improbable that the Lord Buddha can be perceived by means of any physical phenomena. And why? Because, what the Lord Buddha referred to as ‘physical phenomena,’ are not in reality ‘physical phenomena,’ these are merely termed ‘physical phenomena.’”

en.plain: You are working on your appearance, the gym, the clothes, the profile, and it is not making you feel more like yourself.
en.story:
Can the Buddha be seen by his perfect physical body? No; the perfect body is not a perfect body, and is called one. Can he be seen by the fullness of his marks? No; that fullness is not fullness, and is called fullness.

The section says the same thing twice, once about the body and once about its marks, and the repetition is the point: neither the shape nor the finish is where the person is. Work on the body is not wrong; a body that works well is a good thing to have. The section only notes where the work cannot reach. Feeling more like yourself is not a thing the gym or the profile can deliver, because the self they are working on is the one the section says is not the one. Do the work for its own sake, and look for yourself elsewhere.
en.reminder: Neither the shape nor the finish is where you are.
en.acting: Do today's body work for the body's sake, and then do one thing that has nothing to do with how you look.

zh_hant.plain: 你在經營外表，健身房、衣服、個人檔案，這沒有讓你更像自己。
zh_hant.story:
能不能靠圓滿的色身看見佛？不能；圓滿的色身不是圓滿的色身，叫做圓滿的色身。能不能靠具足的諸相看見他？不能；那份具足不是具足，叫做具足。

這一分把同一件事說了兩次，一次關於身體，一次關於它的相，而重複就是重點：形狀和修飾都不是那個人所在的地方。經營身體不是錯；一副好用的身體是好東西。這一分只是指出那份經營到不了的地方。更像自己，不是健身房或個人檔案能交出來的東西，因為它們在經營的那個自己，正是這一分說「不是那一個」的自己。為身體本身做這份工作，然後到別的地方找自己。
zh_hant.reminder: 形狀和修飾，都不是你所在的地方。
zh_hant.acting: 今天為身體本身做身體的事，然後做一件跟外表無關的事。

zh_hans.plain: 你在经营外表，健身房、衣服、个人文件，这没有让你更像自己。
zh_hans.story:
能不能靠圆满的色身看见佛？不能；圆满的色身不是圆满的色身，叫做圆满的色身。能不能靠具足的诸相看见他？不能；那份具足不是具足，叫做具足。

这一分把同一件事说了两次，一次关于身体，一次关于它的相，而重复就是重点：形状和修饰都不是那个人所在的地方。经营身体不是错；一副好用的身体是好东西。这一分只是指出那份经营到不了的地方。更像自己，不是健身房或个人文件能交出来的东西，因为它们在经营的那个自己，正是这一分说「不是那一个」的自己。为身体本身做这份工作，然后到别的地方找自己。
zh_hans.reminder: 形状和修饰，都不是你所在的地方。
zh_hans.acting: 今天为身体本身做身体的事，然后做一件跟外表无关的事。

lines: 即為謗佛不能解我所說故
說法者無法可說是名說法
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “Do not affirm that the Lord Buddha thinks thus within himself, ‘I ought to promulgate a system of Law or doctrine.’ Have no such irrelevant thought! And why? Because, if a disciple affirmed that the Lord Buddha promulgated a system of Law or doctrine, he would defame the Lord Buddha, being manifestly unable to understand the purport of my instruction. Subhuti, regarding the promulgation of a ‘system of Law or doctrine,’ there is in reality no ‘system of Law or doctrine’ to promulgate, it is merely termed a ‘system of Law or doctrine.’” Upon that occasion, the virtuous and venerable Subhuti enquired of the Lord Buddha, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! in ages to come, will sentient beings destined to hear this Law, engender within their minds the essential elements of faith?” The Lord Buddha replied, saying: “Subhuti, it cannot be asserted that these are sentient beings, or that these are not sentient beings. And why? Because, Subhuti, regarding ‘sentient beings,’ the Lord Buddha declared that in reality these are not ‘sentient beings,’ they are merely termed ‘sentient beings.’”

en.plain: You have been explaining, teaching, advising, and you suspect that nobody is actually hearing you.
en.story:
Do not say the Buddha thinks 'I have a teaching to give'; whoever says the Buddha teaches slanders him, for what is taught cannot be grasped and is called teaching. Subhuti asks whether beings in later ages will believe this. The Buddha says they are neither beings nor not beings; beings are not beings, and are called beings.

The section removes the teacher from the teaching. The one who explains and advises all day is doing a real thing, and the suspicion that nobody hears is often correct, because what is heard is rarely the words. What lands, if anything lands, is what the explainer is when not explaining. Say less. Be the thing once, in front of them, and let that be the teaching that cannot be grasped.
en.reminder: What lands is not the words.
en.acting: Give no advice today to one person who usually gets it, and do the thing you would have advised instead.

zh_hant.plain: 你一直在解釋、教、給建議，你懷疑其實沒有人真的在聽。
zh_hant.story:
不要說佛有「我有法可說」的想法；說佛有所說法的人，是在毀謗他，因為所說的法不可取，叫做說法。須菩提問後世的眾生會不會相信。佛說他們不是眾生，也不是非眾生；眾生不是眾生，叫做眾生。

這一分把老師從教法裡拿掉。整天解釋和給建議的人做的是真實的事，而「沒有人在聽」的懷疑常常是對的，因為被聽進去的很少是那些話。真正落下的，如果有東西落下，是解釋的人在不解釋的時候是什麼。少說。在他們面前當那樣東西一次，讓那成為不可取的教法。
zh_hant.reminder: 落下的不是那些話。
zh_hant.acting: 今天對一個平常會得到你建議的人不給建議，改做你本來要建議的那件事。

zh_hans.plain: 你一直在解释、教、给建议，你怀疑其实没有人真的在听。
zh_hans.story:
不要说佛有「我有法可说」的想法；说佛有所说法的人，是在毁谤他，因为所说的法不可取，叫做说法。须菩提问后世的众生会不会相信。佛说他们不是众生，也不是非众生；众生不是众生，叫做众生。

这一分把老师从教法里拿掉。整天解释和给建议的人做的是真实的事，而「没有人在听」的怀疑常常是对的，因为被听进去的很少是那些话。真正落下的，如果有东西落下，是解释的人在不解释的时候是什么。少说。在他们面前当那样东西一次，让那成为不可取的教法。
zh_hans.reminder: 落下的不是那些话。
zh_hans.acting: 今天对一个平常会得到你建议的人不给建议，改做你本来要建议的那件事。

lines: 佛得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
我於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提乃
是名阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
chapters.translation_en: Subhuti enquired of the Lord Buddha, saying: “Honoured of the Worlds! did the Lord Buddha, in attaining to supreme spiritual wisdom, obtain nothing of a real or tangible nature?” The Lord Buddha replied, saying: “In attaining to supreme spiritual wisdom, not a vestige of Law or doctrine was obtained, and therefore it is termed ‘supreme spiritual wisdom.’”

en.plain: You reached the thing you were working toward and, standing there, it feels like nothing much.
en.story:
Subhuti asks: when the Buddha attained supreme awakening, did he attain nothing at all? Yes, says the Buddha: in supreme awakening there is not the smallest thing to be attained; that is why it is called supreme awakening.

The section is the sutra's answer to the anticlimax. The degree conferred, the deposit paid, the finish line crossed, and there is no fanfare inside, only the next morning. The Buddha says this of his own awakening: not the smallest thing was attained. That is not deflation; it is the removal of a false expectation. Attainment was never going to feel like acquiring an object, because it is not one. What you have is what you can now do, and that is felt in the doing, not at the line.
en.reminder: Nothing is acquired at the line; the gain is in what you can now do.
en.acting: Use the thing you attained once today, for its own purpose, and notice that as the reward.

zh_hant.plain: 你到達了一直在努力的那樣東西，站在那裡，感覺沒什麼。
zh_hant.story:
須菩提問：佛得到無上正等正覺的時候，是不是什麼都沒有得到？是，佛說：在無上正等正覺裡，連最小的一點東西都沒有可得的；所以才叫無上正等正覺。

這一分是經對「反高潮」的回答。學位拿到了，頭期款付了，終點線過了，裡面沒有樂隊，只有隔天早上。佛對自己的覺悟這樣說：連最小的東西都沒有得到。那不是洩氣；那是拿掉一個假的期待。得到，本來就不會感覺像拿到一件物品，因為它不是物品。你擁有的是你現在做得到的事，而那是在做的時候感覺到的，不是在終點線上。
zh_hant.reminder: 終點線上什麼都沒有拿到；得到的在你現在做得到的事裡。
zh_hant.acting: 今天為它本來的目的，用一次你得到的那樣東西，把這當獎賞。

zh_hans.plain: 你到达了一直在努力的那样东西，站在那里，感觉没什么。
zh_hans.story:
须菩提问：佛得到无上正等正觉的时候，是不是什么都没有得到？是，佛说：在无上正等正觉里，连最小的一点东西都没有可得的；所以才叫无上正等正觉。

这一分是经对「反高潮」的回答。学位拿到了，头期款付了，终点线过了，里面没有乐队，只有隔天早上。佛对自己的觉悟这样说：连最小的东西都没有得到。那不是泄气；那是拿掉一个假的期待。得到，本来就不会感觉像拿到一件物品，因为它不是物品。你拥有的是你现在做得到的事，而那是在做的时候感觉到的，不是在终点在线。
zh_hans.reminder: 终点在线什么都没有拿到；得到的在你现在做得到的事里。
zh_hans.acting: 今天为它本来的目的，用一次你得到的那样东西，把这当奖赏。

lines: 是法平等無有高下是名
以無我無人無眾生無壽者
則得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
所言善法者如來說即非善法
chapters.translation_en: The Lord Buddha addressed Subhuti, saying: “This Law is coherent and indivisible, it is neither ‘above’ nor ‘below,’ therefore it is termed ‘supreme spiritual wisdom.’ It excludes such arbitrary ideas as an entity, a being, a living being, or a personality; but includes every Law pertaining to the cultivation of goodness. Subhuti, what were referred to as ‘Laws pertaining to goodness,’ these the Lord Buddha declared are not in reality ‘Laws pertaining to goodness,’ they are merely termed ‘Laws pertaining to goodness.’”

en.plain: You compare your practice, your progress, your goodness with other people's, and always come out either ahead or behind.
en.story:
This teaching is level, with no high and no low; that is why it is called supreme awakening. Cultivate every good thing without a self, a person, a being or a life, and awakening follows. And the good things the Buddha speaks of are not good things, and are called good things.

The section says the teaching is level. There is no rung on which one person's practice is above another's, because the whole ladder is the illusion. The comparing mind cannot use a level surface; it needs a slope.
